rv.q: This new take on Lerner and Loewe’s rarely staged Scottish Highlands-set musical is a charmingly whimsical treat.
Reality and dream co-exist in both uneasy and bewitching ways in this sensitive update, even as it unapologetically rests on Lerner’s undeniably barmy book...
Dotty though it is, it's a charmer of a show and it casts a spell.
All was mischievously in tune with this playful and imaginative reworking of the Alan Jay Lerner and Frederick Loewe musical.
It’s a strange fable that feels out of step with the times, however beguiling its dance may be.
There’s enough to admire all the same.
The plot, the characters and the score of Brigadoon melt away like Scotch mist.
So it is song and dance in search of a story.
It’s a wonderful piece of escapism for a summer night, an affectionate embrace of a musical, drizzle or no drizzle.
There is much to enjoy about this production and you cannot help but be utterly charmed by the whispering in the trees and even the suitably Scottish rain on press night.

cn.t: Mixed-to-positive notices for this rare Brigadoon revival at Regent's Park Open Air Theatre. McOnie's choreography and the atmospheric outdoor setting earn praise, though the dated, saccharine material divides critics.
